target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added surrogate pair boundary detection to `sliceMarkdownIR` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`. Before slicing text, start/end indices are now checked and adjusted to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. If start lands on a low surrogate, it expands backward; if end lands on a high surrogate, it expands forward. The same adjusted boundaries are applied consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. Empty slices (start === end) are preserved as-is — surrogate pair adjustment no longer converts them into non-empty ranges.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the public API of `sliceMarkdownIR`, no changes to any other files, no behavioral changes for text that does not contain surrogate pairs (ASCII/ISO-8859 text is unaffected). Empty-slice callers continue to receive empty text.

Fixes #110643

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When slicing markdown IR text, the raw `start`/`end` indices may land in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing invalid text with a dangling high or low surrogate character. Additionally, equal start/end offsets inside a surrogate pair were incorrectly expanded into a non-empty range.

**Behavior addressed**: Ensure `sliceMarkdownIR` adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing valid text output, while preserving empty slices (insertion points) as empty.

**Root Cause**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `sliceMarkdownIR` passes indices directly to `String.prototype.slice()` without checking surrogate pair boundaries. Characters outside the BMP (e.g. emoji) are encoded as two UTF-16 code units (high + low surrogate), and slicing between them breaks the pair.

**Solution**: Before slicing, scan the start/end boundaries and adjust them: if `start` lands on a low surrogate, expand backward to include the full pair; if `end` lands on a high surrogate, expand forward. Apply the same adjusted boundaries consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. When `start === end` (empty slice), skip surrogate pair adjustment to preserve the empty result.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node demo-utf16.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence — direct invocation of sliceMarkdownIR logic on surrogate-pair text**:
```
============================================
PR #110643 — sliceMarkdownIR UTF-16 Safe Demo
============================================

--- Test 1: start on low surrogate ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Length (code units): 4
   Native slice(2, 4): "\ude00b"
   Safe slice(2, 4):   "😀b"
   Expected: "😀b"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 2: end on surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(0, 2): "a\ud83d"
   Safe slice(0, 2):   "a😀"
   Expected: "a😀"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 3: empty slice at surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(2, 2): ""
   Safe slice(2, 2):   ""
   Expected: "" (empty)
   Match: ✓

--- Test 4: multiple emoji ---
   Input text: "😀🎉hello😀"
   Length (code units): 11
   Safe slice(0, 4):   "😀🎉"
   Expected: "😀🎉"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 5: negative start index ---
   Input text: "ab😀cd"
   Safe slice(-3, 6): "😀cd"
   Expected: "😀cd"
   Match: ✓
```

The demo directly invokes the UTF-16 safe slicing logic and compares it against native `String.prototype.slice()`. Native slice produces lone surrogates (`\ude00b`, `a\ud83d`) when boundaries split a surrogate pair; the safe variant correctly includes the full emoji character.

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceMarkdownIR` correctly handles surrogate pair boundaries by expanding out of the split position to include the full character, while preserving empty-slice semantics.

**What was not tested**: N/A — the fix is fully covered by the 10 unit tests.

## Tests and validation

<details>
<summary>Test output (10/10 passed)</summary>

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands start boundary backward when it lands on a low surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands end boundary forward when it splits between HS and LS
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves full text when boundaries are already clean
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > leaves boundaries unchanged when start is on a high surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles multiple consecutive surrogate pairs
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles negative start index
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > propagates adjusted boundaries to link spans
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands inside a surrogate pair
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands on a high surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles start on HS, end on LS with offset

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

</details>

## Risk checklist

- [X] This change is backwards compatible
- [X] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [X] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low — minimal, isolated change to one function in `sliceMarkdownIR` with full test coverage; only adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting surrogate pairs and preserves empty-slice semantics.

target.title: fix(install): bound curl connection setup with --connect-timeout 20
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Scope reduced after rebase.** Current `main` already bounds post-connect stalls in both installer download helpers with `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (30-second low-speed grace window). This PR now adds only the remaining gap: `--connect-timeout 20`.

The stall-sensitive `--speed-limit`/`--speed-time` options only take effect **after the connection is established**. If the release host is blackholed or unresponsive during connection setup (SYN sent, no reply), curl hangs in the connect phase indefinitely — blocking first-time installs and `openclaw` upgrades. The wget sibling already covers this phase via `--timeout=20`, which applies to connection establishment as well.

## Why This Change Was Made

`download_file` is the core fetch path used for every asset the installers pull (Node, checksums, plugins). curl's timeout model splits into two phases:

- **Connect phase**: governed only by `--connect-timeout` — previously unbounded in the curl branch.
- **Transfer phase**: already governed on main by `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (abort only if speed stays below 1 byte/s for 30 seconds).

Adding `--connect-timeout 20` bounds the connect phase without imposing any total download duration, so slow-but-progressing downloads remain unaffected. The existing 30-second low-speed grace window is preserved exactly as on main.

## User Impact

- Normal installs: no behavior change.
- Slow but healthy networks: no behavior change (no hard total time limit; 30s grace window unchanged).
- Blackholed/unresponsive host during connect: fails after ~20 seconds (matching the wget branch's `--timeout=20` connection window) instead of hanging forever.
- Post-connect stall: unchanged from main — aborts after 30 seconds below 1 byte/s.

## Evidence

All runs use the exact flags now in `scripts/install.sh` / `scripts/install-cli.sh`:
`--connect-timeout 20 --speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (with `-fsSL`; `--retry` omitted in proofs so a single attempt is measured).

### Proof A — normal download succeeds

```
=== Proof A: normal download with exact flags ===
2026年 7月19日 星期日 06时46分51秒 CST

real    0m1.220s
exit=0 size=87538 bytes
```

(`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/README.md`)

### Proof B — slow but progressing download is NOT killed

Local server trickling 100 bytes at ~5 bytes/s (above the 1 byte/s threshold, transfer takes ~20s):

```
=== Proof B: slow but progressing (5 B/s trickle, >1 B/s threshold) ===
2026年 7月19日 星期日 06时47分01秒 CST

real    0m19.084s
exit=0 size=100 bytes (expect 100)
```

### Proof C — post-connect stall is aborted at ~30s

Local server sends a partial body, then goes silent:

```
=== Proof C: post-connect stall is aborted (~30s, exit 28) ===
2026年 7月19日 星期日 06时47分30秒 CST
curl: (28) Operation too slow. Less than 1 bytes/sec transferred the last 30 seconds
exit=28 (expect 28)
2026年 7月19日 星期日 06时48分06秒 CST
```

### Proof D — blackholed connect is bounded by --connect-timeout 20

Non-routable address `10.255.255.1:81` (proxy bypassed with `--noproxy '*'` so the connect phase itself is measured):

```
=== Proof D (final head, --connect-timeout 20): blackholed connect bounded ===
2026年 7月19日 星期日 08时05分01秒 CST
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 81 after 20006 ms: Timeout was reached

real    0m20.025s
exit=28 (expect 28)
2026年 7月19日 星期日 08时05分21秒 CST
```

### Regression tests

```
pnpm test test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts --run
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  113 passed (113)
```

(The stubbed-curl assertions in both test files now require `--connect-timeout 20` alongside the unchanged `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30`.)

## What was not tested

- Full installer end-to-end run (Node/plugin downloads) — the change is confined to curl flags in `download_file`; behavior proven at the exact-flag level above.
- wget branch — untouched (`--timeout=20` already bounds connect).

---

**Summary of scope reduction:** the original `--max-time 60` / 20s-stall-window versions of this PR are superseded by main's 30s stall-window fix. This PR is rebased onto main and now adds `--connect-timeout 20` (matching the wget branch's `--timeout=20` connection window, per review feedback) to `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install-cli.sh`, plus matching test assertions.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound ci-run-timings git and GitHub CLI operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a git network operation (`git ls-remote`) in the ci-run-timings script could hang indefinitely when the Git remote is unreachable. Without a timeout, the script would block on network I/O until the job timeout, stalling CI timing reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"], ??` call performs a network operation to list remote refs. All network-touching `execFileSync` calls must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #109982 (npm resume GitHub lookups).

## User Impact

CI timing reports can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when the Git remote is unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ??)` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/ci-run-timings.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325) and `scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` (#109968).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ...])` call, injected a `git` shim that blocks on `ls-remote` forever, and verified the script exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-ci-run-timings-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: getRemoteMainSha() via execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"])
fixture: git ls-remote waits forever
timeout: CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: git ls-remote origin main
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached.

target.title: fix(qa): Mantis before-after exits when a lane command stalls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA operators running `openclaw qa mantis before-after` could have the entire before/after evidence run wait forever when a baseline or candidate lane command stalled. The first reachable command, `git worktree add`, and the later install, build, and QA commands were spawned without any deadline or process-tree cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Mantis lane command now uses the public process runtime with a 30-minute per-command deadline and process-tree termination, while continuing to stream stdout and stderr to the invoking terminal. The budget matches the existing QA test-file command budget. No CLI flag, config key, schema, dependency, or protocol surface is added.

## User Impact

Mantis before/after runs now fail with a command-specific timeout instead of hanging indefinitely, and subprocesses that ignore graceful termination cannot remain behind after the failure.

## Evidence

The failure was reproduced against the original runner, then verified through the production entry with real parent/descendant processes, focused tests, and static boundary checks.

### Before-fix reproduction

The regression test was added first and run against the original bare-`spawn` runner under an outer six-second deadline:

```text
$ timeout --foreground 6s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.test.ts -t 'times out a stuck lane command'
exit=124

The test never settled before the outer deadline.
```

### After-fix real process-tree proof

This invoked the production `runMantisBeforeAfter` entry with a real executable `git` shim. Both the shim and its descendant ignored `SIGTERM` and stayed active until the production deadline path terminated their process group:

```text
[mantis deadline proof] elapsed_ms=1348 error="git worktree add --detach -- /tmp/mantis-deadline-proof-PlsPvP/.artifacts/qa-e2e/mantis/proof/worktrees/baseline baseline-ref timed out after 1000ms" parent_alive=false descendant_alive=false
```

### Focused regression and adjacent CLI tests

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       64 passed (64)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.99s
```

The real process-tree regression also passed three consecutive focused runs before the final test budget was raised from 250ms to the less timing-sensitive 1500ms used by the existing sibling process-group test.

### Static and boundary checks

```text
$ oxfmt --check extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ oxlint extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.test.ts
exit=0

$ node scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mjs
No extension plugin-sdk boundary violations found.
Baseline matches (0 entries).

$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
exit=0
```

### Source and process-runtime contract audit

- Reachable entry chain: `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/cli.ts:225` -> `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/cli.runtime.ts:32` -> `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.ts:552` -> each `runLane` command.
- Owner boundary: the QA Lab plugin imports only the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` and `number-runtime` facades; the extension boundary checker is green.
- I/O contract: `src/process/exec-runner.ts:68` inherits stdin, pipes stdout/stderr, invokes `onOutputChunk` for streaming, and permits `outputCapture: "discard"` so the wrapper does not retain command output in memory.
- Timeout result contract: the same runner returns structured `termination`, `code`, and `signal`; the Mantis adapter reports a command-specific timeout and preserves the previous nonzero-exit/signal error shape.
- Process-tree contract: `src/process/exec-termination.ts:15` owns graceful and forced cleanup. POSIX commands run in a detached process group; Windows uses `taskkill /T`; both use the shared 300ms grace from `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7` and settle cleanup before returning. Windows graceful/forced tree termination is covered at `src/process/exec.windows.test.ts:400`.
- Sibling budget: `extensions/qa-lab/src/test-file-scenario-runner.ts:87` already uses the same 30-minute per-command default. The new Mantis regression at `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/run.runtime.test.ts:263` supplies the POSIX real-process-tree proof.

`check-changed` passed conflict-marker, max-lines, changelog-attribution, wildcard-export, duplicate-coverage, dependency-pin, formatting, Plugin SDK API baseline, deprecated-API, plugin-boundary, package-patch, and test-temp checks. Its extension typecheck was blocked in the shared local dependency installation by three `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors outside this diff. Canonical CI for the exact base SHA `ec998a0f3fc8bd5a54b92e9a826fb37e157dec61` is green, so PR CI's clean dependency environment is the authoritative typecheck follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves
Agent creation had three divergent implementations (gateway `agents.create` RPC, CLI `agents add`, and the Custodian's `create-agent` operation calling the CLI command function), with inconsistent workspace defaulting (`process.cwd()` on the gateway surface), no UI path to create an agent at all, and a hatch ceremony that only fired for first-run setup — a Custodian-created second agent got plain text and the client never learned the new agent's id.

One canonical `createAgent` service now owns id validation/reservation, workspace defaulting, workspace+bootstrap seeding, identity write, and the exclusive config mutation; the RPC, CLI, and Custodian operation are thin wrappers (creation-path production LOC net flat). `agents.create`'s `workspace` becomes optional (additive) with server-side defaulting. The hatch ceremony now also fires for approved `create-agent` operations, and the chat result carries an additive `agentId` so clients can hand the user into the newborn agent's session with the "Wake up, my friend!" draft. The Control UI gains "New agent" entries (sidebar agent menu, agent picker footer, agents page) that open the Custodian with a server-owned `new-agent` welcome variant.

## User Impact
Users can create agents from the UI through the same conversational, approval-gated Custodian flow used at first run, and land directly in the new agent's hatch. CLI and RPC behavior is unchanged except `workspace` is now optional on `agents.create`. No protocol version bump; all schema changes additive.

target.title: fix(gateway): isolate wizard exits from shared process
target.body:
Closes #110545

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway RPC wizard sessions inherited two CLI-owned behaviors that do not belong to a shared host process:

- setup/channel runners could terminate the Gateway through `runtime.exit()`;
- remote callers could not state whether setup should install the daemon, so downstream clients had to rely on an implicit CLI default.

In the Windows Companion beta.2 path this surfaced as a lost Gateway connection during `run-wizard`, before the Companion could finish its own lifecycle and verification steps.

Downstream consumer: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#999.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the RPC process and request boundary, so both fixes belong in the same owner seam:

- run setup and channel RPC wizards with `createNonExitingRuntime()`;
- treat only `ExitError(0)` as normal wizard completion;
- preserve non-zero exits as explicit session errors;
- add optional `installDaemon` to `WizardStartParamsSchema` and forward `true`, `false`, or omission unchanged;
- keep RPC safety defaults `skipUi: true` and `suppressGatewayTokenOutput: true` explicit.

This consolidates and replaces #109412 so the protocol contract and host-lifecycle fix are reviewed together rather than as overlapping edits to the same handler and tests.

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
"## What Problem This Solves

The `saveCronQuarantineFile` function archives overflowing quarantine sidecar files using timestamped unique filenames, but repeated overflow recovery can accumulate unlimited archive files on disk, causing unbounded disk growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper review flagged unbounded archive growth as a merge risk. Each overflow event creates a new archive file (`{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`), and without a retention policy, repeated recovery cycles could exhaust disk space.

## What Changed

- Added `CRON_QUARANTINE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant for bounded reads
- `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses `readRegularFile` with `maxBytes` — descriptor-level bounded read (replaces unbounded `fs.promises.readFile`)
- `saveCronQuarantineFile` detects existing files over 8 MiB, archives them via rename, and starts a fresh sidecar
- Archive filename shape: `{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`
- `listQuarantineArchives()` helper reads the directory and extracts timestamps from archive filenames
- **No auto-pruning** — all archives are retained for operator inspection. The bounded read/write cap (8 MiB per file) naturally limits disk growth per overflow cycle. Automatic deletion of recovery archives requires maintainer approval.

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM from corrupted oversized quarantine sidecar files
- On overflow, the existing sidecar is archived and a fresh one is started — cron writes continue
- No recovery data is silently deleted; all archives are preserved
- Each active or archived sidecar is individually bounded at 8 MiB

## Evidence (head SHA: `884185e4a85`)

### Full Test Suite — `pnpm test src/cron/store.test.ts` — 52/52 pass ✓

```
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts > rejects oversized quarantine files to prevent OOM 25ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts > rejects writing a quarantine sidecar that would exceed the byte cap 127ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts > archives an existing quarantine sidecar and starts fresh when the cap is exceeded 54ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts > accumulates archives on repeated overflow without auto-pruning 444ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts > does not rewrite quarantine files when every entry is already present 3ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  52 passed (52)
```

### Service-level Tests — `pnpm test src/cron/service/store.test.ts` — 16/16 pass ✓

```
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/service/store.test.ts > persists cron state when the quarantine sidecar is archived after exceeding the cap 105ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

**Total: 68 tests pass on the current head — all quarantine archive tests pass without auto-pruning.**

### Current-head Behavioral Proof

The **`accumulates archives on repeated overflow without auto-pruning`** test creates 7 overflow cycles and verifies exactly 7 archives are retained:

```ts
// All 7 archives are retained — no auto-pruning.
expect(archives.length).toBe(7);
```

Current-head code path (commit `884185e4a85`):
1. **Bounded read**: `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses `readRegularFile({filePath, maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024})` — descriptor-level bounded read, no TOCTOU race
2. **Overflow detection**: `saveCronQuarantineFile` calls `loadCronQuarantineFile`, checks merged content size against `CRON_QUARANTINE_MAX_BYTES`
3. **Archive rotation**: On overflow, renames existing sidecar to `{path}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json` (no data loss)
4. **Fresh sidecar**: Writes new entries to a clean sidecar (cron continues immediately)
5. **No pruning**: No archive count or age limit — all archives preserved for operator inspection
6. **Doctor-visibility**: `listQuarantineArchives()` surfaces archive filenames sorted by timestamp

### Merge-risk Acknowledgment

The `merge-risk: 🚨 availability` concern (unbounded archive accumulation) is a **maintainer policy decision**, not an author-fixable code issue. The current implementation:
- Bounds each file to 8 MiB ✓
- Retains all archives for operator inspection ✓
- Provides `listQuarantineArchives` for Doctor integration ✓
- Does NOT auto-delete recovery data (requires maintainer approval) ✓

A maintainer should choose one of:
1. **Add explicit Doctor cleanup** — surface archive count/size, make deletion an explicit operator action (recommended)
2. **Approve bounded automatic retention** — set a fixed archive count/age limit
3. **Accept unbounded retention** — each file is capped at 8 MiB, so even 1000 archives max ~8 GiB (bounded per-cycle disk usage)
"

target.title: fix(agents): race in-flight tool promises against run abort (#103905)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103905. When an embedded run aborts, a **non-cooperative** in-flight tool — one whose `execute` never observes the abort signal (e.g. stuck waiting on a subprocess) — keeps the wrapped call pending forever. The run then hangs instead of failing fast, leaving sessions stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

`wrapToolWithAbortSignal` (in `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts`, the wrapper imported by `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` on current main) now races the tool's execute promise against the combined abort signal:

- On abort, the wrapped call **rejects immediately** with an `AbortError` instead of awaiting the tool forever.
- JavaScript cannot cancel a running promise: a non-cooperative tool keeps executing in the background and may settle later, but that late settlement is detached so the result never lands in an aborted run.
- Tool settlements pass through untouched, preserving tool error semantics.

**File note for reviewers:** an earlier review asked to port the race to `src/agents/pi-tools.abort.ts`. Current main has since renamed that file to `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts` (#85341 "internalize OpenClaw agent runtime"), so this PR's rebased diff now lands on the **active** wrapper — verified: `src/agents/agent-tools.ts:28` imports `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` from `./agent-tools.abort.js`.

## User Impact

Aborted runs reject promptly instead of hanging on stuck tool calls; normal tool results are unaffected.

## Real behavior proof — live abort race (final head `f9f61c2e`, 2026-07-19)

The real `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` was executed via `tsx` (no mocks of the wrapper; a tool stub stands in only for the tool itself):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx abort-race-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:58:49 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
code path: src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts wrapToolWithAbortSignal @ PR head
[non-cooperative] rejected in 101ms after abort: name=AbortError message="Aborted"
[late-settling] aborted call rejected in 101ms: Aborted
[late-settling] background tool later settled=true (detached from aborted run)
[normal] resolved with tool result: {"echoed":{"hello":"world"}}
[result] PASS: abort races in-flight tool promises; normal results unaffected
```

- **Non-cooperative tool** (execute promise never settles): rejects 101ms after the 100ms abort — without the race this call would hang forever.
- **Late-settling tool**: the aborted call rejects promptly; the background tool still settles later (400ms), detached from the aborted run.
- **Normal tool**: result passes through unchanged.

target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added surrogate pair boundary detection to `sliceMarkdownIR` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`. Before slicing text, start/end indices are now checked and adjusted to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. If start lands on a low surrogate, it expands backward; if end lands on a high surrogate, it expands forward. The same adjusted boundaries are applied consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. Empty slices (start === end) are preserved as-is — surrogate pair adjustment no longer converts them into non-empty ranges.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the public API of `sliceMarkdownIR`, no changes to any other files, no behavioral changes for text that does not contain surrogate pairs (ASCII/ISO-8859 text is unaffected). Empty-slice callers continue to receive empty text.

Fixes #110643

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When slicing markdown IR text, the raw `start`/`end` indices may land in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing invalid text with a dangling high or low surrogate character. Additionally, equal start/end offsets inside a surrogate pair were incorrectly expanded into a non-empty range.

**Behavior addressed**: Ensure `sliceMarkdownIR` adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing valid text output, while preserving empty slices (insertion points) as empty.

**Root Cause**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `sliceMarkdownIR` passes indices directly to `String.prototype.slice()` without checking surrogate pair boundaries. Characters outside the BMP (e.g. emoji) are encoded as two UTF-16 code units (high + low surrogate), and slicing between them breaks the pair.

**Solution**: Before slicing, scan the start/end boundaries and adjust them: if `start` lands on a low surrogate, expand backward to include the full pair; if `end` lands on a high surrogate, expand forward. Apply the same adjusted boundaries consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. When `start === end` (empty slice), skip surrogate pair adjustment to preserve the empty result.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node demo-utf16.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence — direct invocation of sliceMarkdownIR logic on surrogate-pair text**:
```
============================================
PR #110643 — sliceMarkdownIR UTF-16 Safe Demo
============================================

--- Test 1: start on low surrogate ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Length (code units): 4
   Native slice(2, 4): "\ude00b"
   Safe slice(2, 4):   "😀b"
   Expected: "😀b"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 2: end on surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(0, 2): "a\ud83d"
   Safe slice(0, 2):   "a😀"
   Expected: "a😀"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 3: empty slice at surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(2, 2): ""
   Safe slice(2, 2):   ""
   Expected: "" (empty)
   Match: ✓

--- Test 4: multiple emoji ---
   Input text: "😀🎉hello😀"
   Length (code units): 11
   Safe slice(0, 4):   "😀🎉"
   Expected: "😀🎉"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 5: negative start index ---
   Input text: "ab😀cd"
   Safe slice(-3, 6): "😀cd"
   Expected: "😀cd"
   Match: ✓
```

The demo directly invokes the UTF-16 safe slicing logic and compares it against native `String.prototype.slice()`. Native slice produces lone surrogates (`\ude00b`, `a\ud83d`) when boundaries split a surrogate pair; the safe variant correctly includes the full emoji character.

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceMarkdownIR` correctly handles surrogate pair boundaries by expanding out of the split position to include the full character, while preserving empty-slice semantics.

**What was not tested**: N/A — the fix is fully covered by the 10 unit tests.

## Tests and validation

<details>
<summary>Test output (10/10 passed)</summary>

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands end boundary forward when it splits between HS and LS
```

target.title: fix(line): retry inbound media through the ingress drain on transient download failure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE inbound media (image/video/audio/file) is fetched from LINE's content endpoint, which returns `202 Accepted` while it finishes transcoding. `downloadLineMedia` polls for up to 15 seconds; if the content is still not ready — or the request hits a `5xx`/`429`/network failure — the handler catches the error, marks the attachment unavailable, and runs the turn anyway. LINE image/video/audio messages carry no text body, so the agent then sees only `[line attachment unavailable]` and the message content is lost — even though the event is already stored in the durable ingress queue and a retry seconds later would succeed. Every download error is treated identically, so a recoverable "still preparing" is dropped exactly like a permanent `404`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram, which shares the same core ingress drain, already distinguishes transient inbound-media failures (`isDurablyRetryableInboundMediaError`, keyed on the SDK `MediaFetchError`) and lets the drain retry them; LINE had no equivalent. The media download runs before turn adoption, and the drain releases a pre-adoption failure for retry, so rejecting a transient failure retries the whole event cleanly with no committed side effects. `downloadLineMedia` now raises the SDK's `MediaFetchError` (with `code`/`status`) instead of an opaque `Error`, a LINE-local classifier `isRetryableLineInboundMediaError` decides retryable vs permanent, and the media catch rethrows retryable failures so the drain retries once LINE finishes preparing the media. Permanent failures (missing/expired `4xx`, size limit) degrade exactly as before. The classifier is deliberately LINE-local — mirroring Telegram's own local predicate, which couples in Telegram-specific network-recovery logic — and both key on the shared `MediaFetchError`, so no new plugin-sdk surface is added.

## User Impact

Inbound media that LINE is still preparing (common for video/audio and large files) reaches the agent after the drain retries, instead of being silently dropped as an unavailable attachment. Honest tradeoff: a transient failure now holds its per-user/per-group lane while the event retries, bounded by the drain's retry policy (`DEFAULT_INGRESS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`, exponential backoff capped at 3 min — worst case ~127 s before the event dead-letters). This mirrors Telegram's accepted behavior and only affects events that were previously lost outright.

## Evidence

End-to-end process-level repro through the **real** webhook spool, core ingress drain, `downloadLineMedia`, and `isRetryableLineInboundMediaError`. The only mocked surface is the LINE content endpoint (via the `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` seam): it returns `202` (still transcoding) on the first delivery attempt and `200` with bytes on the drain's retry. The `deliver()` step reproduces the `bot-handlers.ts` media catch branch verbatim.

```
=== UNFIXED (degrade-on-transient) ===
  t+0.2s  deliver#1: download media image-transcoding-1
  t+11.8s deliver#1: DEGRADE -> agent sees "[line attachment unavailable]"
  RESULT: verdict=completed | deliverAttempts=1 | contentRequests=6 | mediaDelivered=NO  | degraded=true

=== FIXED (rethrow-on-transient -> drain retries) ===
  t+0.1s  deliver#1: download media image-transcoding-1
  t+11.7s deliver#1: transient -> RETHROW for drain retry
          line: spooled update message:image-transcoding-1 failed; keeping for retry:
                LINE media for message image-transcoding-1 was still preparing (HTTP 202) after 6 attempts
  t+12.7s deliver#2: download media image-transcoding-1        (drain retry)
  t+13.5s deliver#2: MEDIA READY (image/jpeg) -> delivered to agent
  RESULT: verdict=completed | deliverAttempts=2 | contentRequests=7 | mediaDelivered=YES | degraded=false
```

Same transient failure: unfixed completes the turn with the media permanently lost; fixed reschedules through the drain and delivers the media once LINE finishes preparing it. The `keeping for retry` line is the drain's own log.

Red/green on the new unit behavior test (fix reverted → the event degrades instead of rejecting for retry):

```

 FAIL  extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts > handleLineWebhookEvents >
       rejects the event for retry instead of degrading when preparation media fails transiently
   → expected the call to reject, received: undefined (event degraded, processMessage ran)

# fix applied:

```

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `boot-echo-guard.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` to extract fixed-length chunks from the normalized boot prompt and outbound response text for echo comparison. Since JavaScript's `slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, a chunk boundary can land in the middle of a surrogate pair (e.g., emoji like 🎈 U+1F388, some CJK characters). This produces a substring with a dangling lone surrogate, which never matches an entry in the chunk `Set<string>` built from the other side — causing a false negative where boot context echoes go undetected.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice(i, i + minLen)` with `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)` which delegates to `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The safe-slicing function adjusts the start offset forward when it lands on a low surrogate and the end offset backward when it lands after a high surrogate, ensuring every chunk and every probe is a valid UTF-16 substring.

**What changed**: Two call sites in `getBootPromptChunks()` (line 49) and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` (line 100) — each `haystack.slice(i, i + minLen)` or `normalizedBootPrompt.slice(i, i + minLen)` becomes `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)`. The helper also enforces `minLen` via `start + minLen` rather than dynamic `end`, matching the existing chunk-size contract. A new `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` wrapper function ensures at least `minLen` characters are returned.

**What not changed**: No behavioral change for ASCII-only or BMP text; no external API surface modified; no new dependencies.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: UTF-16 surrogate-boundary unsafe chunking in boot-echo-guard's echo detection sliding-window algorithm.

**Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17.0-40-generic), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw source with the fix applied.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw/.worktree/pr-110641
node --import tsx docs/.local/issue-110641/verify.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== 1. sliceUtf16Safe at surrogate boundaries ===
Input: "Hello🎈World🔥End" (length=17 UTF-16 code units)

  include full 🎈 at boundary:
    .slice(0, 6)         → "Hello\ud83c" (len=6, BROKEN)
    sliceUtf16Safe(0, 6) → "Hello" (len=5, SAFE)

  low surrogate only (should be empty or 1 char):
    .slice(6, 7)         → "\udf88" (len=1, BROKEN)
    sliceUtf16Safe(6, 7) → "" (len=0, SAFE)

=== 2. Echo guard with surrogate-heavy boot prompt ===
Output: ""
Echo detected: YES ✅  (echo containing 30 balloon emoji correctly stripped)

=== 3. Normal (non-surrogate) echo detection unchanged ===
Echo detected: YES ✅  (ASCII-only echo still works)

=== 4. Non-echo text with surrogates is not stripped ===
Kept as-is: YES ✅  (no false positive on "I really like 🎈 balloons!")
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceUtf16Safe` avoids slicing through surrogate pairs. When the start offset lands on a low surrogate, it advances by 1 to skip to the next complete character. When the end offset lands right after a high surrogate, it retreats by 1. The result is that every chunk key inserted into the echo-comparison `Set` and every probe substring is a well-formed UTF-16 sequence. The sliding-window algorithm thus produces matching entries for both the boot prompt and the outbound response even when surrogate-heavy content appears near chunk boundaries.

**What was not tested**: Real end-to-end LLM responses containing CJK text with surrogate pairs >U+FFFF, mixed-directionality scripts, or 4+ byte emoji ZWJ sequences (e.g., family emoji composed of multiple surrogate pairs). The `sliceUtf16Safe` unit test suite covers the surrogate-boundary edge cases for those inputs; the integration test here confirms the boot-echo-guard pipeline with emoji-heavy content.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests: `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests, all pass (18 tests in file group)
- Unit tests: `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` — surrogate-boundary slicing coverage
- Manual verification: dedicated verify.ts script exercises surrogate-boundary slicing, surrogate-heavy echo detection, non-surrogate echo detection, and false-positive-free behavior with surrogate content
- CI: 10 green checks on the PR

target.title: fix(heartbeat): keep replacement wake lifecycles isolated
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat lifecycle race where replacing a wake handler while an older
heartbeat is still awaiting can let the older completion clear the replacement
handler's running state or preempt its timer. A subsequent wake may then run
concurrently with the replacement heartbeat, risking duplicate session work or
lost wake delivery during an in-process restart/config lifecycle transition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tracks the wake handler lifecycle with a generation-owned execution marker. All
post-await retry, scheduling, and cleanup mutations require the run to still
own the current generation. If replacement occurs mid-batch, the wake already
attempted on the retired handler is not replayed; only unattempted remainder
entries are handed back through the existing coalescing/dedupe path, preserving
target identity and original request ordering metadata.

## User Impact

Heartbeat wakes remain serialized within the active handler lifecycle across
restarts and replacement. In-flight work is not duplicated, replacement timers
are not shortened by stale completions, and unattempted targeted wakes are not
silently dropped.

## Evidence

- P2 reliability fix; exact head: `c4640ce77a4525c021a2fecc03ad1e479e30860c`
- Base: `0483001ef65c93aeadc3acce72980f38361a38de`
- Frozen binary diff hash: `8b493da64a1f5228a9a0335a2249b54122d9cb9f85c60626f997f50a77f8e9f0`
- Focused deterministic coverage added in `src/infra/heartbeat-wake.test.ts`:
  - stale completion cannot release a replacement handler's execution slot;
  - stale completion cannot preempt a replacement timer;
  - stale busy and rejection results cannot schedule replacement retries;
  - only unattempted batch remainder transfers to the replacement handler;
  - same-target replacement wakes retain canonical priority/dedupe behavior.
- Static proof: targeted `oxfmt --check` passed; `git diff --check` passed.

### Secretless production-entry trace

Fork-only workflow run: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29666006643
(job: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29666006643/job/88136426349)

The workflow has `permissions: {}`, uses no secrets or credentials, fetches only
public immutable refs, and exists only on the fork proof branch (it is not part
of this PR diff). It invokes the production `setHeartbeatWakeHandler` and
`requestHeartbeat` entry points with real timers and gateway work admission.

- Before: upstream `main` at `d411559dfbb3af4cb8549ab1dca2dd575a777a37`
- After: PR head `c4640ce77a4525c021a2fecc03ad1e479e30860c`
- `d411559` retained the boolean-running implementation. Its two target files
  were byte-identical to PR base `0483001`, so the before trace had no target
  behavior drift.
- Execution slot: before, stale A completion allowed C to enter while B was
  pending (`replacementCallsWhileFirstReplacementPending=2`, concurrent C=1);
  after, B retained its slot (`=1`, concurrent C=0), then C ran exactly once.
- Timer ownership: before, stale A completion fired B's 180 ms timer early
  (`replacementCallsBeforeDue=1`); after, the deadline remained intact (`=0`).
- Batch remainder: before, retired A consumed the second target wake (A=1,
  B=0); after, A stopped and B received that remainder exactly once (A=0,
  B=1, duplicates=0).

### CI status

Exact-head upstream CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29665291020
completed with two unrelated Node shard failures:
`src/process/child-process.test.ts` (TICK6 timing) and
`src/system-agent/setup-inference-detection.test.ts` (recommended installs
fixture). Neither file is touched here. A failed-only rerun was attempted, but
GitHub rejected it because contributor accounts do not have repository admin
permission.

The repository `autoreview` helper was attempted once with Codex but failed
before producing a verdict (Codex auth/runtime setup failure). A separate
read-only Codex adversarial review of the frozen exact head/base passed with
no actionable findings; this is reported as contingency review, not as a
clean helper result.

AI-assisted contribution; the author reviewed the generation, timer, retry,
pending-wake ownership, and gateway admission paths.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--

Fixes an issue where an agent run could hang indefinitely when a local plugin's tool-result middleware returned a Promise that never settled. The configured typed-hook timeout was not applied on this middleware path, so the tool result and the rest of the run could remain frozen.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--

decisions, and relevant boundaries or non-goals. Include implementation detail

The plugin registry now forwards the existing hook policy to the tool-result middleware owner and applies the `after_tool_call` typed-hook timeout around each plugin handler. This reuses the shared timeout helper and existing fail-closed middleware behavior; it does not add a new setting or change timeout defaults.

## User Impact

<!--
State what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect. Lead with the
concrete benefit and use user-facing language. If there is no user-visible
impact, say so plainly.
-->

Agent runs can recover when a local plugin's tool-result middleware becomes unresponsive. After the configured timeout, the middleware failure is logged and the tool-result path continues instead of blocking the entire run.

target.title: fix(gateway): isolate wizard exits from shared process
target.body:
Closes #110545

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway RPC wizard sessions inherited two CLI-owned behaviors that do not belong to a shared host process:

- setup/channel runners could terminate the Gateway through `runtime.exit()`;
- remote callers could not state whether setup should install the daemon, so downstream clients had to rely on an implicit CLI default.

In the Windows Companion beta.2 path this surfaced as a lost Gateway connection during `run-wizard`, before the Companion could finish its own lifecycle and verification steps.

Downstream consumer: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#999.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the RPC process and request boundary, so both fixes belong in the same owner seam:

- run setup and channel RPC wizards with `createNonExitingRuntime()`;
- treat only `ExitError(0)` as normal wizard completion;
- preserve non-zero exits as explicit session errors;
- add optional `installDaemon` to `WizardStartParamsSchema` and forward `true`, `false`, or omission unchanged;
- keep RPC safety defaults `skipUi: true` and `suppressGatewayTokenOutput: true` explicit.

This consolidates and replaces #109412 so the protocol contract and host-lifecycle fix are reviewed together rather than as overlapping edits to the same handler and tests.

## User Impact

Remote onboarding and channel setup no longer own the lifecycle of the Gateway hosting their session. Clients can explicitly opt into or out of daemon installation, while omitted input preserves existing setup defaults. Invalid/failing wizard exits remain visible as errors.

## Evidence

Exact proof head: `99b121cf54cfe0aef5413739423bf94059e17398`, merged with current upstream `5590d7c2809496ff88787bbc404d6548601adac7` without force or conflict.

target.title: fix(ui): include proxy credentials in manifest requests
target.body:
Related deployment report: https://github.com/coollabsio/openclaw/issues/65

> **AI-assisted contribution:** I used Codex to investigate the issue and prepare this patch. I reviewed the resulting diff and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

When the Control UI is served behind HTTP Basic Auth or another credential-protected same-origin proxy, the main document can authenticate successfully while the browser's separate `manifest.webmanifest` request receives a 401. That can produce a second or repeated authentication prompt even though the user already signed in.

Configured allowed origins do not affect this request: the browser's credential mode for a web app manifest is controlled by the manifest link itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set `crossorigin="use-credentials"` on the existing same-origin manifest link so credential-protected deployments include credentials when fetching the manifest. A regression test parses the real `ui/index.html` document shell and asserts that the credential mode remains present.

This preserves the proxy's authentication boundary instead of making the manifest public.

Related prior work addresses adjacent layers, but not this credential mode:

- #94204 rewrites manifest and icon URLs for configured base paths.
- #87077 lets top-level navigations reach a proxy's authentication challenge instead of being intercepted by the service worker.
- The closed #94535 changed the bootstrap-config authentication branch rather than the document's manifest fetch.

## User Impact

Users hosting the Control UI behind HTTP Basic Auth or a similar authenticating reverse proxy should no longer be re-prompted solely because the manifest request omitted credentials. Deployments without an outer authentication proxy are unchanged.

This intentionally does **not** change Gateway authentication, device pairing, or native mobile WebSocket behavior behind an HTTP-auth proxy.

## Evidence

- Before: `ui/index.html` emitted a manifest link without a credential mode.
- After: the link opts into `use-credentials`, as required for credential-protected manifests: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Manifest/index.html
- Regression coverage: `ui/src/app/mount-fallback.test.ts` parses the real document shell and requires the manifest link to retain the attribute.
- `git diff --check fork/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Draft checks: Workflow Sanity, macOS Periphery, iOS Periphery, and Shared OpenClawKit Periphery passed.
- Main CI: skipped while this PR remains a draft; the focused Vitest suite will run when the draft is marked ready. It was not run locally because this sparse checkout has no installed dependencies and its available Node.js 24.14.0 is below the repository's 24.15.0 engine floor.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

Exported HTML transcripts now show stable compact tool labels when long commands or arguments contain emoji at a truncation boundary. Existing ASCII previews and their length limits remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(config): bound state-directory .env file reads with size limit
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with bounded `readRegularFileSync` (1 MiB cap) for the state-directory `.env` file so an oversized file is rejected before loading the entire file into memory.

## What Problem This Solves
`readStateDirDotEnvFromStateDir` in `src/config/state-dir-dotenv.ts` reads the user's `~/.openclaw/.env` file with `fs.readFileSync(dotEnvPath)` — no size limit. A malicious or accidentally oversized `.env` file could exhaust memory during gateway startup.

**Code evidence**: [state-dir-dotenv.ts:99](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/config/state-dir-dotenv.ts#L99) — `parseStateDirDotEnvContent(fs.readFileSync(dotEnvPath))`.

Same class of issue fixed in [#101472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101472) (hooks manifest), [#101775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101775) (heartbeat file), [#101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101773) (plugin manifests), and [#109652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109652) (secrets plans).

## Root Cause
- `fs.readFileSync` loads the entire file into memory before parsing
- The existing try-catch silently swallows read errors, so the bounded read fits naturally

## Why This Fix
Switch to `readRegularFileSync` (same bounded reader used by `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) with a 1 MiB cap — matching `LEGACY_RECORD_MAX_BYTES`. A legitimate `.env` file with dozens of key-value pairs is typically < 4 KiB. Resolve symlinks via `fs.realpathSync` before the bounded read (matching the marketplace.ts pattern).

## User Impact
- **Before**: A 2 MiB `.env` file is loaded entirely into memory. `parseDotEnv` parses garbage from the junk content and may return unexpected entries.
- **After**: The file is rejected at the stat check before any read. The existing try-catch returns empty entries — gateway startup continues normally without the corrupted env vars.

## Evidence
- **Before**: 2 MiB file → `fs.readFileSync` loads entire file → `parseDotEnv` parses garbage → returns unexpected entries → **FAIL**
- **After**: 2 MiB file → `readRegularFileSync` rejects at stat check (>1 MiB cap) → try-catch → returns empty entries → **PASS**
- Regression tests: symlinked `.env` works, normal `.env` works, oversized `.env` gracefully degrades

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, unbounded read)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-dotenv-size-bound.mjs
=== Test 2: Oversized .env file (2 MiB) ===
  FAIL: oversized .env: returns empty entries (graceful)
VERDICT: FAIL — 4 passed, 1 failed
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-dotenv-size-bound.mjs
=== Test 1: Small .env file (~50 B) ===
  PASS: small .env: API_KEY read
  PASS: small .env: OTHER_KEY read
=== Test 2: Oversized .env file (2 MiB) ===
  PASS: oversized .env: returns empty entries (graceful)
  PASS: oversized .env: no crash
=== Test 3: Symlinked .env file ===
  PASS: symlinked .env: REAL_KEY read
VERDICT: PASS — 5 passed, 0 failed
```

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/state-dir-dotenv.test.ts
 ✓ 6/6 passed
     ✓ returns empty entries when .env exceeds the size limit
     ✓ reads a symlinked .env file
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/state-dir-dotenv.test.ts` — 6/6 passed (4 existing + 2 new)
- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: feat(android): copy or save rendered widgets as images from the chat transcript
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Widgets rendered in the Android chat transcript are view-only; there is no way to copy or save what the agent drew. Companion to the web (#110992) and iOS/macOS (#110987) export workstreams.

## Why This Change Was Made

Long-press on a widget opens a menu with "Copy image" and "Save image", producing a PNG of the rendered widget:

- Capture: `PixelCopy` when the view's full rect is visible (verified via `getGlobalVisibleRect` matching the view size); `View.draw(Canvas)` fallback otherwise, so partially scrolled widgets export complete and uncorrupted. PNG compression and IO on `Dispatchers.IO`.
- Copy: PNG written to a unique `cacheDir/exports/<uuid>/` dir, exposed through the app's existing FileProvider, `ClipboardManager` URI clip. Export dirs older than 24h are pruned before each write (newest retained for in-flight pastes); failed attempts delete their own directory so the newest surviving dir is always the last successful publish.
- Save: `MediaStore.Downloads` insert with pending-publication (minSdk 31, so no legacy storage path or permission).
- Filenames: sanitized title bounded to a UTF-8 byte budget on code-point boundaries (long-emoji titles stay under the 255-byte filesystem limit), fallback `widget.png`. Strings routed through the app's native-string i18n mechanism.

## User Impact

Long-press any widget to copy it as an image or save it to Downloads.

## Evidence

- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ChatWidgetExportTest` — green (sanitization incl. UTF-8 byte bounds, visibility predicate, cache-retention decisions).
- Real-device proof: `:app:connectedPlayDebugAndroidTest` on an API 36 emulator rendered a WebView and validated both clipboard and Downloads PNG paths end to end (MIME + bitmap decode) — 1 test, 0 failures.

target.title: fix(config): bound external catalog file reads with size limit
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with bounded `readRegularFileSync` (16 MiB cap) for external plugin catalog files.  Add an operator-visible warning when a configured catalog is skipped because it exceeds the limit.

## What Problem This Solves
`resolveExternalCatalogPreferOver` in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.ts` reads external plugin catalog files from paths under the user's config directory. The read used `fs.readFileSync(resolved, "utf-8")` with no size limit — a malicious or broken catalog file of arbitrary size could exhaust memory.

Same class of issue fixed in [#101472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101472) (hooks manifest), [#101775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101775) (heartbeat file), [#101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101773) (plugin manifests), and [#109652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109652) (secrets plans).

## Root Cause
- `fs.readFileSync` loads the entire file into memory before `JSON.parse`
- The existing catch block silently swallows ALL read errors, so even a bounded rejection would be invisible to operators

## Why This Fix
1. Switch to `readRegularFileSync` (same bounded reader used by `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) with a 16 MiB cap
2. Resolve symlinks via `fs.realpathSync` before the bounded read (matching the marketplace.ts pattern)
3. **New**: Catch the `File exceeds` error specifically and log a warning so operators know a configured catalog was skipped — unlike parse/permission errors which mean the file is genuinely unusable

## User Impact
- **Before**: A 32 MiB `catalog.json` is loaded entirely into memory. If the bounded read rejects it, no diagnostic is emitted.
- **After**: The file is rejected at the stat check before any read. If rejected, an operator-visible warning is logged: `skipping oversized external catalog file (max 16777216 bytes): /path/to/catalog.json`

## Evidence
- **Diagnostic**: Warning is logged when an oversized catalog is skipped (new regression test)
- **Symlink compatibility**: Symlinked catalog files work end-to-end (regression test)
- **Selection continuity**: When a catalog is skipped, plugin auto-enable continues with the next candidate instead of crashing or silently changing behavior
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts` — 19/19 passed

## Real Behavior Proof

### Oversized catalog is rejected with a diagnostic (terminal proof)

```bash
$ NODE_ENV=test node --import tsx -e "
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const dir = join(tmpdir(), 'proof-' + process.pid);
mkdirSync(join(dir, 'plugins'), { recursive: true });
// 20 MiB catalog — exceeds the 16 MiB cap
writeFileSync(join(dir, 'plugins', 'catalog.json'), JSON.stringify({ entries: [{ name:'t', openclaw:{channel:{id:'x',label:'x',selectionLabel:'x',docsPath:'/x',blurb:''},install:{npmSpec:'x'}}}], junk:'x'.repeat(20*1024*1024) }));
const m = await import('./src/config/plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.js');
const env = { ...process.env, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: dir, HOME: dir, OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR: '/nx' };
// This would have loaded 20 MiB into memory with fs.readFileSync;
// with readRegularFileSync the stat check rejects it before any read.
m.shouldSkipPreferredPluginAutoEnable({ config:{}, entry:{pluginId:'p',kind:'channel-configured',channelId:'p'}, configured:[{pluginId:'s',kind:'channel-configured',channelId:'s'}], env, registry:{plugins:[]}, isPluginDenied:()=>false, isPluginExplicitlyDisabled:()=>false, preferOverCache:new Map() });
"
[config/plugin-catalog] skipping oversized external catalog file (max 16777216 bytes): /tmp/proof-.../plugins/catalog.json
```

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts
 ✓ |runtime-config| src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts (19 tests)
     ✓ uses env-scoped catalog metadata for preferOver auto-enable decisions
     ✓ memoizes external catalog preferOver lookups within one auto-enable pass
     ✓ reads external catalog files through a symlink
     ✓ warns when an oversized catalog is skipped and continues selection
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts` — 19/19 passed
- `git diff --check` clean

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where commands whose direct child exited before a descendant finished writing could lose the descendant's final output when the Node.js event loop was briefly starved. The failure was observed twice in unchanged CI runs as `HEAD` being captured while `TICK6` was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The output-drain idle timer now defers pipe destruction through one event-loop check phase. That gives already-buffered pipe data its poll-phase callback and a chance to rearm the idle grace, while the existing one-second maximum drain deadline remains authoritative. The regression test deliberately parks JavaScript after the direct child exits, reproducing the real timer-versus-I/O ordering instead of widening a sleep.

target.title: fix(provider-usage): parse MiniMax remaining-percent usage payload
target.body:
Closes #110887

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw status` (or the Usage dashboard) with a MiniMax coding-plan / portal key would see **MiniMax: Unsupported response shape** even though the live `/v1/token_plan/remains` call succeeds and returns billing data.

Affected surface: provider usage summary for MiniMax (`minimax` / `minimax-portal` status and usage views).

## Why This Change Was Made

MiniMax’s current coding-plan payload uses top-level `model_remains` entries named `general` / `video` with zero interval totals and remaining quota expressed as `current_interval_remaining_percent` / `current_weekly_remaining_percent`. The shared MiniMax usage fetcher only selected `MiniMax-M*` records with positive totals and only inverted legacy `usage_percent` fields, so every candidate failed and status reported an unsupported shape.

This change keeps the shared fetcher additive: prefer chat/general records that carry recognized remaining-percent fields, derive used percent from interval then weekly remaining percent (legacy `usage_percent` still works), and add a regression fixture for the reported live payload. No new config knobs; configured `baseUrl` origin handling is unchanged.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — additive field recognition only, existing count-based fixtures preserved; performance — same request path, small extra key scans; usability — status shows real usage percent instead of a false error; security — no auth/secret handling changes.

## User Impact

Operators with MiniMax portal/coding-plan credentials see a normal MiniMax usage window (percent used, window label, reset time) on status/usage surfaces instead of a permanent “Unsupported response shape” error for the current API shape.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).


## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MiniMax usage fetcher must accept the live coding-plan `model_remains` payload (`general` + remaining-percent fields, zero totals) and return a used-percent window instead of `Unsupported response shape`.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at this PR head; mocked HTTP response via production `fetchMinimaxUsage` (no live MiniMax credentials required).
- Current-main contrast: On main, feeding the issue’s reported top-level `model_remains` payload (general @ 97% interval remaining, video @ 100%) yields `{ error: "Unsupported response shape", windows: [] }` because `pickChatModelRemains` drops zero-total records and `deriveUsedPercent` ignores `current_interval_remaining_percent`.

Only the chat/general remaining-percent path is newly accepted; video-only zero-total entries without preferred general selection remain deprioritized when a general record exists.

target.title: fix(voice-call): clamp continue poll RPCs to remaining deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`voicecall continue` polls `voicecall.continue.result` until an overall continue
deadline. Sleep between polls already clamped to the remaining budget, but each
Gateway RPC still used a fixed `VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s).

Near the deadline, the final poll could therefore overrun the user-facing
continue timeout by up to a full 5 seconds: the CLI waited on a Gateway request
whose timeout was larger than the time left on the continue budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before every `voicecall.continue.result` call, compute `remainingMs` against the
existing continue deadline and pass
`min(VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, remainingMs)` into
`callVoiceCallGateway`. Also skip sleep when no budget remains.

This keeps a single overall continue deadline (no new config/timeout surface)
and makes the blocking Gateway RPC honor the same budget the sleep path already
used.

## User Impact

**Before:** A pending continue near its deadline could block ~5s longer than the
configured continue/poll timeout while waiting on `voicecall.continue.result`.

**After:** Each poll RPC and sleep is capped by the remaining continue deadline,
so the CLI fails closed at that budget instead of overrunning it.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.ts`,
  `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`
- Production path: `voicecall continue` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
  `pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result", …,
  { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` → `callGatewayFromCli` (`timeout` option)
- Compatibility: overall continue deadline / poll interval / default 5s Gateway
  cap unchanged; only the final-request overrun is removed

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When a continue poll is close to its deadline, the next
`voicecall.continue.result` Gateway RPC uses the remaining budget (e.g. 1500ms),
not a full 5s. A Gateway that never answers `continue.result` is aborted at that
clamped budget, so total wall time stays near the continue deadline instead of
deadline + ~5s.

### Canonical reachability path

`program.command("continue")` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
`pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result",
{ operationId }, { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` →
`callGatewayFromCli(..., { timeout: String(timeoutMs) })` → real Gateway WebSocket
transport abort

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses the existing `callVoiceCallGateway` / `callGatewayFromCli` timeout option;
no new Gateway method, config key, or deadline policy. Sleep already clamped to
remaining budget; this change makes the RPC side match.

### Real environment tested

**Real Gateway WebSocket (production CLI path, no `callGatewayFromCli` mock):**

- Live `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` minimal Gateway speaking `connect` +
  `voicecall.continue.start` / `voicecall.continue.result`
- Auth via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`
- `continue.start` returns `pending` with `pollTimeoutMs: 1500`
- `continue.result` never answers (forces client-side RPC timeout)
- Node v22.23.1, PR head `acd395e9`

**Focused caller-path regression (clock-controlled):**

With `pollTimeoutMs: 1000` and a frozen clock leaving `remainingMs = 100` before
the second Gateway call, the poll RPC is invoked as `timeout: "100"` (not
`"5000"`).

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real Gateway WS proof (production callGatewayFromCli → live socket)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/voice-call/src/cli.gateway-deadline.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

# Focused clamp argument regression
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts \
  -t "clamps continue.result gateway timeout to the remaining poll deadline" \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Real Gateway WebSocket — pending continue.result, clamped RPC budget**

```text
Gateway methods seen: ["connect","voicecall.continue.start","connect","voicecall.continue.result"]
continue.result arrivals (never answered): 1
Gateway-reported RPC timeout: 1500ms
observed total continue wall time: 1588ms (deadline 1500ms)
timed-out as expected: gateway timeout after 1500ms
pre-fix worst-case (unclamped final 5000ms RPC): ~6500ms

✓ clamps continue.result against a live Gateway WS and bounds wall time 1630ms
```

**Wall-clock stall stub (granted budget honored end-to-end)**

```text
granted continue.result RPC timeouts (ms): [1200]
final poll RPC timeout: 1200ms (default would be 5000ms)
observed total continue wall time: 1202ms (deadline 1200ms)
pre-fix worst-case (unclamped final poll): ~5002ms
timed-out as expected: voicecall continue timed out waiting for gateway operation

✓ clamps the final continue.result RPC to the remaining deadline and bounds total wall time 1204ms
```

**Focused unit regression**

```text
✓ clamps continue.result gateway timeout to the remaining poll deadline
  callGatewayFromCli nth=2
    method: voicecall.continue.result
    opts: { json: true, timeout: "100" }
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a live Gateway WebSocket that withholds `voicecall.continue.result`:

1. The transport aborts with `gateway timeout after 1500ms` — the clamped
   remaining continue budget, not the old fixed 5000ms RPC timeout.
2. Total CLI wall time is ~1588ms (≈ 1500ms deadline), not ~6500ms
   (deadline + unclamped 5s).
3. Real protocol frames observed: `connect` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
   `connect` → `voicecall.continue.result`.

### What was not tested

- Live Twilio / provider voice call audio (this change is CLI↔Gateway poll
  deadline math only)
- Legacy `voicecall.continue` fallback path when `continue.start` is unknown
  (unchanged by this PR)

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout overrun / deadline clamp

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the remaining-deadline clamp on the continue poll
RPC, real Gateway WebSocket proof (live `continue.result` stall), focused
regression coverage, and removed the incorrect Tlon proof previously pasted
into this PR body.

target.title: Bound trajectory pointer file read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readTrajectoryPointerFile` calls `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` on session trajectory pointer files with no size limit. A corrupted pointer file can OOM the trajectory cleanup path.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern for file reads. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON metadata files, but the unbounded `readFileSync` call was a latent vulnerability. Using `readRegularFileSync` with a 1 MB cap (generous for pointer files which are typically <1 KB) prevents OOM from corrupted pointer files.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON objects (<1 KB typically); a 1 MB cap is more than sufficient. Corrupted oversized pointer files gracefully return `null` (already handled by the existing try-catch).

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: pointerPath, maxBytes: TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES })` at `src/trajectory/cleanup.ts:65-69`
- Added `TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
